summary: Pole tower built 1946 per Lands and Mines annual reports; Alberta Wildfire's layer lists a steel tower at the site built in 2012, 30 m tall.

facts.design: Pole tower with a lumber cupola in 1946; the Alberta layer lists the present structure as a steel tower

events.note: Six miles of road built to the Heart Lake tower-site (annual report, fiscal year ending 31 March 1944)
Pole tower completed in summer 1946; a later report (year ending 31 March 1947) gives it as 76 ft high with a lumber cupola
Four 50-foot radio masts erected at the tower (report for the year ending 31 March 1948)
Year of construction for the steel tower now listed at the site, per the Alberta layer. The sources do not say whether it replaced the 1946 tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Alberta Wildfire's layer gives 30 m for the steel tower (TOWER_HEIGHT 30.0). OpenStreetMap, a volunteer-edited map, tags the Heart Lake Fire Tower at 50 m with lattice construction. The story uses the layer's figure and reports the OSM tag as a disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Not established: whether the 2012 steel tower stands on the 1946 site. The Canada Lookouts entries give the 1946 site only by its land description (Section 29-68-9-W4). The layer coordinates (54.915, -111.340) and OSM coordinates (54.914, -111.335) are about 0.3 km apart, which does not settle it. Staffing, access and current condition are not in any source read, so they are left out. The brief's elevation (866.0 m) matches the layer's 866.05 m. Searches: 2 WebSearch, which turned up no 2012 record and no tower history beyond the Canada Lookouts transcriptions; search snippets are not cited. Page reads: 3 (Canada Lookouts, Alberta layer query, OpenStreetMap node). No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-20: 'provincial' removed (the Canada Lookouts page does not say it); the story now gives metric before feet throughout; the 'status: standing' fact was dropped because no cited source describes current condition.
